definition: A system composed of multiple AI agents that interact, communicate, or collaborate (and sometimes compete) to accomplish tasks.
details: Multi-agent LLM systems can divide labor across specialized sub-agents (e.g., a planner, a coder, a reviewer), potentially improving robustness and task decomposition compared to a single monolithic agent.

explainer.lead: A multi-agent system is a set of AI agents that interact, communicate, or collaborate, and sometimes compete, to accomplish tasks. It matters because splitting work across specialized agents can improve robustness and task decomposition over one monolithic agent.

tiers.eli5: Think of a team where one person plans, one writes the code, and one checks the work. They talk to each other and each does their part instead of one person doing everything.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers build multi-agent LLM systems by dividing labor across specialized sub-agents such as a planner, a coder, and a reviewer. The aim is better robustness and decomposition than a single monolithic agent.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as a system composed of multiple AI agents that interact, communicate, or collaborate (and sometimes compete) to accomplish tasks. Stated benefit is potentially improved robustness and task decomposition versus a single agent.

explainer.example: A planner agent outlines the task, a coder agent implements it, and a reviewer agent checks the output before it is returned.
